title: Start here
summary: What the pieces are and how a day flows through Noto.

sections.heading: The three things you need to know
sections.body: Noto keeps you honest about what you actually finish. Everything else is detail.

points.label: Workspace
points.text: A container for one area of your life. Each has its own items, mode and stats.

points.label: Mode
points.text: How a workspace looks and pushes you. It never changes what is stored.

points.label: Today
points.text: One logical day per workspace. It can start at 04:00 if your nights run late.

sections.heading: The loop
sections.body: Noto is built around a small daily rhythm rather than an endless list.

points.label: Capture
points.text: ⌘K or the field at the bottom of Today. Type a sentence; tokens like ~30m or !2 are understood.

points.label: Morning review
points.text: Decide what today holds. Carried items are put in front of you, one at a time.

points.label: Work
points.text: Pick a Now item with f. Only one at a time, so the day has a focus.

points.label: Shutdown
points.text: Close the day: say what got done and what carries.

points.label: Weekly review
points.text: Once a week, sweep what has gone stale.

sections.heading: Where to go next
sections.body: Press ⌘K and type a word — the guide itself is searchable, as is every screen.

points.label: Confused by a control
points.text: Most controls have a small ⓘ next to them that opens the matching page here.

points.label: Confused by a number
points.text: Open an item and read its Age, Carry and Defers — explained under "Age, carry, defers".

title: Workspaces
summary: One container per area of your life.

sections.heading: What a workspace isolates
sections.body: Items, history and tags; the mode (layout, order, pressure); stats; sync; time zone, day boundary, focus hours and daily capacity.

points.label: New workspace
points.text: Sidebar → New workspace. The templates (Work, Personal, Health, Side Projects) are one-click starting points.

points.label: Switch
points.text: Click it, or press ⌘1…⌘9.

points.label: Rename / delete
points.text: Settings → Workspace.

sections.heading: Focus hours
sections.body: Focus hours separate contexts in time as well as in data.

points.label: Outside focus hours
points.text: The workspace drops out of Today (all) and its badge goes quiet. Nothing is hidden if you open it directly.

points.label: Quick capture
points.text: Defaults to the workspace whose focus hours are active.

sections.heading: Capacity and the day
sections.body: Two settings that quietly shape what Today shows.

points.label: Daily capacity
points.text: How much you can realistically take on. Today's capacity bar compares your planned work against it.

points.label: Day boundary
points.text: When a new day begins, e.g. 04:00. Work done at 01:00 still counts for yesterday.

points.label: Time zone
points.text: Follow the device, or pin the workspace to a zone so a trip does not reshuffle your days.

title: Modes, presets, layout, order, pressure
summary: A mode is three independent controls. The named modes are just bundles of them.

sections.heading: A mode is three controls, not one
sections.body: Earlier versions had six monolithic modes, which contradicted each other. A mode is now three independent controls, and the six named modes are presets over them.

points.label: Layout
points.text: How items are arranged: list, board, timeline or habit grid.

points.label: Order
points.text: How items are sorted inside their section.

points.label: Pressure
points.text: How loudly Noto reminds you: gentle, honest or relentless.

points.label: Preset
points.text: A named bundle of the three. Picking one just sets all three at once.

sections.heading: Changing a mode never edits your items
sections.body: Switching layout, order or pressure is presentation only. It writes nothing to items, so you can experiment freely and switch back.

points.label: Items without the layout's field
points.text: They are never dropped. A timeline item with no date sits in a "No date" lane; a board item with no column sits in Someday.

points.label: Rollover
points.text: Identical in every mode, because rollover is a query over the same data.

points.label: Custom
points.text: Change any one control and the preset reads "sprint (custom)". Change it back and the label follows.

sections.heading: The six presets
sections.body: Each is a starting point, not a commitment.

points.label: Sprint
points.text: list · priority + carry · honest — work and daily throughput.

points.label: Zen
points.text: list (spacious) · manual · gentle — personal, low pressure.

points.label: Deadline
points.text: timeline · due date · honest — exams, launches, time-boxed projects.

points.label: Habit
points.text: habit grid · time of day · gentle — health and routines.

points.label: Kanban
points.text: board · manual · gentle — side projects and multi-phase work.

points.label: Accountability
points.text: list · carry · relentless — any workspace where you want the truth.

sections.heading: How to change it
sections.body: Sidebar → Settings → Mode, or press ⌘K and type "Switch preset".

title: Layouts
summary: List, board, timeline or habit grid.

sections.heading: What each layout does
sections.body: The layout decides the shape of the home screen. The items are the same in all four.

points.label: List
points.text: Sections Now / Planned / Waiting on / Done today, plus a Backlog for Unscheduled and Someday.

points.label: Board
points.text: Columns Someday · Backlog · Today · Waiting · Done. Dragging sets status and planned date — no hidden extra state.

points.label: Timeline
points.text: Items with a due date or a future plan are placed on a line; overdue items are pinned on top; the rest wait in "No date".

points.label: Habit grid
points.text: Shows repeating rules with missed days skipped. Everything else is one click away under "Not habits".

sections.heading: Each layout remembers its own setup
sections.body: Board columns, timeline range and the grid's window are stored per layout, so switching away and back restores them.

title: Order
summary: How items are sorted inside a section.

sections.heading: The five strategies
sections.body: Sections (Now, Planned, Waiting, Done) are always applied first; order sorts within a section.

points.label: Manual
points.text: Keeps the order you dragged things into.

points.label: Priority + carry
points.text: Priority first, then how long it has been carried.

points.label: Due date
points.text: Overdue first, then nearest due date; undated items last.

points.label: Carry
points.text: Most-carried and oldest first — the honest view.

points.label: Time of day
points.text: Morning → Midday → Afternoon → Evening, then your manual order.

title: Pressure
summary: How loudly Noto reminds you — and how much it does on its own.

sections.heading: Carry, not age
sections.body: Every threshold is measured in carry: the number of planned days that passed with the item undone. An item added today is fresh however old its due date is.

points.label: Gentle
points.text: No left bar, review is optional. Fresh 0–4, warm 5–9, hot 10–13, stale 14+. Stuck at carry 14 or 5 defers.

points.label: Honest
points.text: Review is on. Fresh 0, warm 1–2, hot 3–5, stale 6+. Stuck at carry 3 or 3 defers.

points.label: Relentless
points.text: Review cannot be skipped and your 3 most-carried items are pinned on top. Stuck at carry 2 or 2 defers.

sections.heading: What pressure never does
sections.body: It does not change what is stored and it does not shame you. A missed day is an empty square, never a red cross.

title: Age, carry, defers
summary: The three numbers in the inspector, and what the colours mean.

sections.heading: The three numbers
sections.body: Select an item and they appear on the right. They are the honest core of Noto.

points.label: Age
points.text: Days since the item was created. A plain fact; nothing escalates on age alone.

points.label: Carry
points.text: Days the item was planned for and left undone. This is what pressure reacts to.

points.label: Defers
points.text: Times you explicitly pushed it to a later day.

sections.heading: The states
sections.body: The same item can be warm in one workspace and stale in another, because the thresholds are the workspace's pressure setting.

points.label: Fresh
points.text: Ordinary text colour. Nothing to see.

points.label: Warm
points.text: A gentle amber tint on the carry mark.

points.label: Hot
points.text: Amber bar on the left edge of the row.

points.label: Stale
points.text: Red bar, and the row says "stuck?".

sections.heading: "Stuck?" is a question, not a verdict
sections.body: When an item crosses the stuck threshold, Noto asks why instead of nagging: too big, blocked, waiting, not important, or forgotten.

points.label: Break it down
points.text: Splits it into steps so the next action is obvious.

points.label: Make it Now
points.text: Commits the next 25 minutes to it.

points.label: First thing tomorrow
points.text: A deliberate one-day defer — it will not be counted as carry twice.

title: Editing, deleting, restoring
summary: Change any field of a task, and get anything back.

sections.heading: Everything is editable
sections.body: Select a task and the inspector on the right lists its fields. Changing one runs the same action the keyboard does — nothing is a special case.

points.label: Title
points.text: Type a new one and press Enter, or click away.

points.label: Time
points.text: An estimate: 15 min, 30 min, 1 hr, 1.5 hr… It counts against today's capacity.

points.label: Priority
points.text: 1 is highest. It decides the order when the workspace sorts by priority.

points.label: When
points.text: Today, tomorrow, in a week, Someday, or Unscheduled.

points.label: Due
points.text: A deadline. Overdue items are pinned on top in the Deadline layout.

points.label: Day part
points.text: Morning, midday, afternoon or evening — used by the habit grid's order.

points.label: Waiting on
points.text: Name who or what is blocking it; the task moves to Waiting on.

points.label: Notes
points.text: Free markdown.

sections.heading: Every change is recorded
sections.body: Each edit is written to the item's history, which is what "Life of this item" at the bottom of the inspector shows — with the values, not just that something changed:

points.label: Example
points.text: estimate 30m → 1h · priority none → P2 · due Oct 12 → no date

points.label: Why keep it
points.text: It is how Noto answers "why is this still here?" without guessing.

points.label: Undo
points.text: Every change is one ⌘Z. Nothing here needs a confirmation dialog.

sections.heading: Deleting
sections.body: Nothing is ever destroyed outright.

points.label: Delete a task
points.text: Inspector → Delete task. The row leaves your lists, and ⌘Z brings it straight back.

points.label: Drop is different
points.text: Dropping (⌫) keeps the task and records why you let it go; deleting hides it entirely.

title: Morning review
summary: The one-at-a-time decision pass that starts your day.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Noto puts every carried item in front of you, one at a time, and asks for a decision. It exists because a list you never decide on is just a wish.

points.label: When it opens
points.text: Once a day, unless the workspace is on gentle pressure or you dismissed it. ⌘⇧R opens it any time.

points.label: Nothing to review
points.text: It tells you so and gets out of the way.

points.label: Undo
points.text: Every decision is undoable — ⌘Z.

sections.heading: The decisions
sections.body: Each has a single key, so the whole review is one hand on the keyboard.

points.label: T — Today
points.text: Commit it to today.

points.label: D — Defer
points.text: Push it to a specific day.

points.label: S — Someday
points.text: Off today's plate, still alive.

points.label: B — Break down
points.text: Turn it into smaller steps.

points.label: W — Waiting on
points.text: Blocked on someone; asks who.

points.label: X — Drop
points.text: Let it go. It is not a failure.

points.label: A — Already done
points.text: It happened; record it without carrying it.

title: Shutdown
summary: The three-step end of the day.

sections.heading: Why it exists
sections.body: The day ends deliberately rather than by running out of attention. Shutdown records what happened and what carries, then closes.

points.label: Step 1
points.text: What got done today.

points.label: Step 2
points.text: What is still open, and where it goes.

points.label: Step 3
points.text: One line about the day, kept for the weekly review.

points.label: Later
points.text: Press ⌘⇧D to run it whenever you are stopping.

title: Weekly review
summary: The once-a-week sweep for things that have gone quiet.

sections.heading: Five steps
sections.body: It looks back at the week and forward to the next, and gives you one place to clear the backlog.

points.label: Completed
points.text: What you actually finished.

points.label: Someday
points.text: Promote it, keep it, or drop it. Anything untouched for 60+ days is pre-selected for dropping.

points.label: Stuck
points.text: Grouped by why it stalled, so you can fix the cause rather than each item.

points.label: Estimate vs focus
points.text: How well your time estimates held up.

points.label: Outcomes
points.text: Up to three outcomes for next week. They are pinned to the header all week.

title: Today (all)
summary: Every workspace's today in one list, and why some disappear.

sections.heading: The cross-workspace lens
sections.body: ⌘0 shows today across all workspaces at once. Rows carry their workspace's colour so you can tell them apart.

points.label: Why a workspace is missing
points.text: It is outside its focus hours, so it is quiet. Open it directly and everything is still there.

points.label: Capacity
points.text: Committed time against capacity, summed across the workspaces that are in focus.

title: Capture
summary: Get it out of your head in one line.

sections.heading: Where to capture
sections.body: ⌘K from anywhere, or the field at the bottom of Today. The same tokens work in both.

points.label: ~30m
points.text: An estimate in minutes (also ~2h).
Priority 1–4.

points.label: tomorrow / fri / 12 Oct
points.text: A planned or due day.

points.label: @waiting:name
points.text: Mark it as waiting on someone.

points.label: in Personal
points.text: File it in another workspace by name.

points.label: #tag
points.text: A tag.

sections.heading: Attach what you are looking at
sections.body: When a browser is in front, quick capture offers to attach the current page to the item.

title: Keyboard shortcuts
summary: The keys worth knowing. Press ? for this list at any time.

sections.heading: Global
sections.body: These work from anywhere except while typing in a text field.

points.label: ⌘K
points.text: Ask or jump — search items, run commands, or add one.
Switch workspace.
Today across all workspaces.

points.label: ⌘T / ⌘⇧R / ⌘⇧D
points.text: Jump to today / start review / shut down.

points.label: ⌘I / ⌘B
points.text: Toggle the inspector / the sidebar.

points.label: ⌘Z
points.text: Undo the last action.

points.label: ⌘⇧M
points.text: Open the mode settings.

sections.heading: In a list
sections.body: Move with j/k or the arrow keys.

points.label: x
points.text: Complete.

points.label: e or Enter
points.text: Edit the title.

points.label: f
points.text: Make it Now.

points.label: t / d / s / w
points.text: Today / Defer / Someday / Waiting on.

points.label: b / ⌫
points.text: Break down / drop.
Set priority. ~ sets an estimate.
Previous / next day.

title: Connected apps
summary: Why a row can show "2 approved" or "CI passing".

sections.heading: What the chips are
sections.body: When an item links to a pull request or issue, Noto shows a few facts from the host as chips on the row. They are read-only — a glance, not a control panel.

points.label: Approvals
points.text: How many reviewers have approved.

points.label: Checks
points.text: The CI result, if the host reports one.

points.label: State
points.text: Open, ready to merge, or closed.

points.label: Reconnect
points.text: If a token expires the chip says so; reconnecting is done from Settings.
